Respondent :- State Of Up And 2 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Kripa Shankar Shukla

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Yash Padia Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

Heard Shri Kripa Shankar Shukla, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Shri Yash Padia, learned counsel for respondent No. 3.
2.

The petitioner has assailed the order dated 27.03.2024 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer (Joint Organisation), Varanasi, by which the application/representation of the petitioner purported to be under Section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been rejected on the ground that the land of the petitioner is situated in a different village, land of which falls under category "Bhumi Ghan-2", whereas the land in respect of which award was passed by the Court Manisha Devi vs State Of Up And 2 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101584825/
1 dated 12.08.2011, was in respect of a different village, where the land falls in category "Bhumi Palo-3"
3.

entities.text: Manisha Devi vs State Of Up And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the subject land of the petitioner was acquired by same notification under Section 4 of the Act dated 23.11.2001.
He submits that in such circumstances, the reasoning given for rejecting the application under Section 28-A of the Act is manifestly erroneous.

4. Section 28 -A of the Act reads as follows:
"28A. Re-determination of the amount of compensation on the basis of the award of the Court. -

(1) Where in an award under this part, the Court allows to the applicant any amount of compensation in excess of the amount awarded by the Collector under section 11,
the persons interested in all the other land covered by the same notification under section 4, sub-section (1) and who are also aggrieved by the award of the Collector may, notwithstanding that they had not made an application to the Collector under section 18, by written application to the Collector within three months from the date of the award of the Court require that the amount of compensation payable to them may be re-determined on the basis of the amount of compensation awarded by the Court:
Provided that in computing the period of three months within which an application to the Collector shall be made under this sub-section, the day on which the award was pronounced and the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the award shall be excluded.

(2) The Collector shall, on receipt of an application under sub-section (1), conduct an inquiry after giving notice to all the persons interested and giving them a reasonable opportunity of being heard, and make an award determining the amount of compensation payable to the applicants.

(3) Any person who has not accepted the award under sub-section (2) may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court and the provisions of sections 18 to 28 shall, so far as may be, apply to such reference as they apply to a reference under section 18."

5. For applicability of Section 28-A, the requirement is that a person praying for re-determination should have his land covered by the same notification under Section 4 in respect whereof, there has been an enhancement of compensation by the Court in case of some other person.
It is wholly immaterial that the land of the claimant is situated in a different village so long as it is covered by the same notification under Section 4 of the Act.

Consequently, the reasoning given in the impugned Manisha Devi vs State Of Up And 2 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101584825/
2 order is manifestly erroneous in law.

entities.text: Manisha Devi vs State Of Up And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In case, there is difference in the nature of land so covered by the same notification, it is open to the Collector while holding enquiry as envisaged under sub-section (2) of Section 28-A to consider the said aspect and award compensation accordingly, but it cannot constitute a ground for summarily rejecting the application under Section 28-A of the Act.
7.
Consequently, the impugned order is hereby quashed.
8. The matter is remitted back to the second respondent to hold enquiry as regards enhanced amount of compensation payable to the petitioner keeping in mind the nature of land.
9. The aforesaid exercise shall be completed within three months from the date of communication of the instant order.
10. In the result, the instant petition stands allowed to the extent indicated above.
